primitives.name: Fatigue-Optimized Batting Practice
primitives.verbatim_quote: 206 WALTER CAMP'S BOOK OF COLLEGE SPORTS more demoralizing to a good pitcher than to keep him pitching for batting practice, until he becomes tired and careless.
primitives.assumptions: Pitcher fatigue increases linearly with time; optimal batting practice ends before fatigue-induced error rate exceeds threshold.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When P(T) > 0.8, practice efficacy degrades significantly.

layer2.mapping: Models the inverse relationship between pitcher fatigue and practice effectiveness via a logistic decay function.
layer2.telemetry: Error rate in pitch recognition and swing timing during practice sessions.

primitives.name: Uniform Hit Distribution
primitives.verbatim_quote: Each man should be given a certain number of hits, until all have had a turn.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'H_i': 'number of hits assigned to player i', 'N': 'total number of players', 'T': 'total hits distributed'}
primitives.assumptions: All players receive equal opportunity; hit distribution is uniform across participants.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When H_i ≠ T/N, practice fairness is compromised.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to a discrete uniform distribution over player indices, ensuring equitable exposure.
layer2.telemetry: Number of times each player receives a hit during practice cycle.

primitives.name: Simulated Game State Transition
primitives.verbatim_quote: Then let the playing be as if it were a regular game.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S_t': 'state vector at time t', 'R': 'game rules (fixed)', 'P_{ij}': 'probability of transition from state i to j'}
primitives.assumptions: Practice simulates full game mechanics with fixed rule set and probabilistic transitions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When S_t deviates beyond R, simulation fidelity fails.

layer2.mapping: Maps practice state transitions to a Markov chain with absorbing states representing game completion.
layer2.telemetry: Transition frequency between defensive/attacking configurations during practice.

The first primitive establishes a fatigue-aware model where pitcher endurance directly impacts practice quality—a key dualistic constraint. The second introduces a fairness kernel through uniform hit allocation, ensuring no player is disadvantaged in exposure. The third primitive formalizes the shift from controlled drills to emergent gameplay, enabling state-space exploration. These primitives form a triadic structure: fatigue control ensures sustainability, equity ensures participation, and simulation enables adaptation. Failure modes include overtraining leading to decreased performance, unequal access causing disengagement, and premature simulation leading to poor tactical integration. The interplay of these constraints creates a bounded optimization landscape for team preparation.
